metadata.name: Liberal Conservatism (Australian tradition)
metadata.description: The Australian synthesis of liberal rights, private enterprise, constitutional government and established civic institutions. Party principles are evidence of this scoped tradition, not a substitute for examining doctrinal disagreements.
metadata.period: Australia: Liberal Party federal platform adopted April 2002
metadata.scope: The Australian synthesis of liberal rights, private enterprise, constitutional government and established civic institutions. Party principles are evidence of this scoped tradition, not a substitute for examining doctrinal disagreements. Revision2 is an incomplete evidence audit of this specified school. Unsupported modern applications and empirical causal comparisons are null/unknown. Neither agreement nor neutrality is inferred from silence. Historical or programme sources are not a complete contemporary incumbent-government record. The federal party’s July 2026 immigration statement supplies a dated contemporary application. It is an opposition proposal, not an implemented incumbent act; its numerical and causal allegations are not adopted as facts.
metadata.phrase: A society protecting enterprise and individual rights while sustaining family, community and constitutional institutions.
